description:
`jobs/transport.rs` derives a position's type by looking the value up in
`facts.analysis().value_types` and defaulting a miss to `any`. That default is
the fz-f98.17 defect: a hole becomes a wrong answer the cumulative join can
never retract, and the callsite ends up holding two disagreeing facts.

fz-f98.18 removed two of them (the entry-capture pair, now `entry_capture_ty`,
proven dead across lib + matrix before being converted to an invariant) and
fz-hwn.27.5 had already converted the resume-payload one (`resume_payload_ty`).
TEN remain:

    272, 292, 307, 352, 1080, 1090, 1331, 1358, 1441, 1482

## The sharpest one first

Line ~352 and `resume_payload_ty` (~1290) derive the type of the SAME position
kind -- `TransportPosition::ResumePayload` -- and disagree: one defaults to
`any`, the other panics naming `key_is_value_template`. One position kind, two
answers. Collapse them onto the strict one.

## Method that worked in fz-f98.18

Replace the default with `unwrap_or_else(|| panic!(...))`, run `cargo test --lib`
and `cargo test --test fixture_matrix -- --test-threads=1`, and count probe hits.
Zero hits across both is evidence the default is dead and can become an
invariant. A hit is evidence the value can legitimately be absent -- in which
case say WHY in place, and say what the right answer is (`none` for a dead
position is usually it, never `any`).

## Checks

- Each of the ten is either removed or carries a comment justifying it with the
  evidence above.
- The two ResumePayload derivations are one derivation.
- Full lib + matrix at baseline or better.
title: Audit the ten remaining unwrap_or_else(any) type defaults in transport.rs
